# The data model

<!-- GENERATED by tooling/scripts/gen/data-model.mjs. Do not edit: regenerate. -->

Every table in the `public` schema, as the migrations leave it: its columns, its keys, whether row-level security
is on and what each policy lets through, and the module in `packages/db/src` that reads and writes it (the files
that name it in a `.from("…")`; "none" when no repository names it). It is written from `supabase/schema.sql`, the schema
dumped from a replay of every migration, which also holds the functions, triggers, indexes and grants this page
leaves out, and every policy's expression in full. A partition is listed under its parent.

After a migration, with `supabase start` running: `corepack pnpm gen:schema-snapshot`, then
`corepack pnpm gen:data-model`. `tests/docs/data-model.test.mjs` fails when this page is not
what the script writes.

## Tables

### ad_accounts

The owner's own ad account on one platform, connected once (decision 0049, 00648): the platform and its id for the account, its name, currency (ISO 4217) and time zone (IANA), where the connection stands, what the platform says the account stands on, the platform's own ids beside it, who connected it and when, and how its last read went. Its token is a Vault secret, ad-creds-<id>, reached only through ad_credentials_put, _get and _drop: no column holds it or says where it is. One live account a platform in a workspace, and a platform's account is held by one workspace at a time. Members read; every write is a door's.

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/ads/accounts.ts`
- Primary key: `id`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| Column | Type | Null | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | uuid | no | `gen_random_uuid()` |  |
| `tenant_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `platform` | text | no |  |  |
| `external_id` | text | yes |  |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |  |
| `currency` | text | yes |  |  |
| `timezone` | text | yes |  |  |
| `status` | text | no |  | choosing: signed in, and two accounts could both be the one, so the owner is asked. connected: read, and its ads can be paused. revoked: the platform took access back (revoked_at); the last numbers stay, and nothing is read or changed until it is connected again. disconnected: the owner disconnected it (disconnected_at); its ads stay as they last were. |
| `standing` | jsonb | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | What the platform says the account stands on, in typed words only: for Meta, account (active, disabled, unsettled, review, grace, closing, closed) and funding (ok, none). Empty until the first read. A check a page draws is read from this and from config in one place (contracts). |
| `config` | jsonb | no | `'{}'::jsonb` | The platform's own ids and facts beside the account, one shape a platform, read by contracts: for Meta the business portfolio, the Page the ads run as and its name, the WhatsApp number and the Instagram account that Page is linked to, the account's own spending limit and its least daily amount, the accounts to choose from while one is to be chosen, and what its token was granted. Never a token. |
| `token_expires_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `connected_by` | uuid | yes |  |  |
| `connected_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `revoked_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `disconnected_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `withdrawn_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the platform confirmed that Chanlytics' access is withdrawn there, after a disconnect. Null until it does: until then a page says where the owner can remove Chanlytics themselves, and never that access is withdrawn. |
| `read_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `read_error` | text | yes |  |  |
| `usage_pct` | numeric(5,2) | yes |  |  |
| `usage_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `read_after` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | The moment before which the platform is not asked about this account again: its own word of when a slowed caller may return, or what its usage figures leave. Null where nothing holds a read back. |
| `notices_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `created_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `updated_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `next_read_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the account is next read at its platform (00650): written by each read, an hour on, or fifteen minutes on while one of its ads is being checked or is in its first two days. Null until its first read, which is due at once. |
| `settle_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the account's next fourteen-day look back is due (00650): once a day, at four in the morning in its own zone. The read that finds it due re-reads those days and marks the ones before them settled. |
| `rung_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the bell last looked at the account's ads (00658): each good read rings what turned since, and stamps it. Null, or older than connected_at, until the first look after a connect, which rings nothing. |
| `most_minor` | bigint | yes |  | The most the owner said any ad may cost, in this account's minor units (00659; the Ads plan's G6), said once in a sentence to AI. Null until they say one: a draft's amount is then never above the largest total turned on. Written only by ad_account_most. |

Foreign keys:

- `tenant_id` → [`tenants`](#tenants) (`id`), on delete cascade

| Policy | For | To | Using | With check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ad_accounts_member_select` | select | authenticated | `(tenant_id IN ( SELECT m.tenant_id FROM memberships m WHERE (m.user_id = auth.uid())))` |  |

### ad_days

The platform's day for one ad, in the account's own zone (decision 0049 call 3, 00648): what it spent, in whole minor units of the account's currency, how often it was shown and tapped, and the platform's own count of what the ad asks for. The platform's half only: who an ad brought and who booked are worked out from contacts and the visits record at each read and kept nowhere. Kept 25 months. Members read; the read's door writes.

- Owned by: none
- Primary key: `ad_id`, `day`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| Column | Type | Null | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenant_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `ad_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `day` | date | no |  |  |
| `spend_minor` | bigint | no | `0` |  |
| `impressions` | bigint | no | `0` |  |
| `clicks` | bigint | no | `0` |  |
| `platform_results` | bigint | yes |  |  |
| `read_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `settled` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether the platform's numbers for the day have stopped moving. A platform keeps correcting a day for about two weeks, so a figure with an unsettled day in it says "so far" (contracts adCostRule). |

Foreign keys:

- `tenant_id`, `ad_id` → [`ads`](#ads) (`tenant_id`, `id`), on delete cascade
- `tenant_id` → [`tenants`](#tenants) (`id`), on delete cascade

| Policy | For | To | Using | With check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ad_days_member_select` | select | authenticated | `(tenant_id IN ( SELECT m.tenant_id FROM memberships m WHERE (m.user_id = auth.uid())))` |  |

### ad_drafts

A workspace's one draft of a new ad (00659; the Ads plan's 4.6, 6.2 and G18): what New ad chose and the ad writer's words, for the ad account it was drafted for. Members read it; ad_draft_keep writes it. Never trusted: every read, and Turn on's press, judges it afresh from the business as it stands.

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/ads/drafts.ts`
- Primary key: `id`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| Column | Type | Null | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | uuid | no | `gen_random_uuid()` |  |
| `tenant_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `account_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `draft` | jsonb | no |  | What New ad chose, as server/ads/draft-shape.ts holds it: the service by its name, the picture's file id, the miles, the amount in minor units, the end day, the words (three versions or none) and the answers to Meta's special-kind question. |
| `kept_by` | uuid | yes |  | The member who kept it last (auth.uid() at ad_draft_keep): the owner, or someone who left it for the owner. |
| `created_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `updated_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `writing_ask` | uuid | yes |  | The ask out for the draft's words, while one is (00672): written by ad_draft_writing, let go by ad_draft_written. Null where no writer is out. |
| `writing_for` | text | yes |  | The words that ask writes, as the dashboard names them (00672; server/ads/writer.ts): the service, the picture, and whether they say the price. Another ask for the same words waits for it. |
| `writing_until` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | Until when another ask for the same words waits for the one out (00672): within the words route's own minute. Past it, the next ask writes its own. |

Foreign keys:

- `tenant_id`, `account_id` → [`ad_accounts`](#ad_accounts) (`tenant_id`, `id`), on delete cascade
- `tenant_id` → [`tenants`](#tenants) (`id`), on delete cascade

### ad_entries

One row each time someone reaches a workspace through an ad (decision 0049, 00644): the platform and its own id for the ad, the kind of entry, whether it made the person, the message that carried it, and what the ad said. Its person is its message's. Written by one door, ad_entry_keep: opened by the first-touch trigger in the message's own transaction, its words kept by the edge afterwards. It enriches and counts nothing: counts of people per ad read contacts.acquired_via and acquired_ref. No click id is kept. Members read; the service role writes.

### ads

### contact_marks

Per member per person: seen_at is how far the member has seen of the person, in the customer's own moments (the last_inbound_at their screen held as they opened the thread or the page), unread_at when they put it back as unread, cleared by the next opening, and marked_at when the row was last written (00349). ### deals

One engagement a person is deciding on or has taken (0004): proposed (a proposal out), won (a client), lost (passed), ended. Written by deal_record on a person's word, an Ask card through the same route, or a payment webhook later (source); never by the receptionist. A stage is an assertion, so no guard: every move is an event and version refuses a stale press. One open engagement (proposed or won) per person per service.

### file_archives

One copy of a Library file, a file and an origin (the archive PRD 1.1, 00686). saved: a copy the owner saved to their Google Drive on a press; it is theirs and is never read back. picked: the owner's own Drive file a pick brought in. shelf: Chanlytics' own copy. A video's copy at the video platform may be let go only behind a checked shelf copy, a picked origin or a watched folder's item. Its connection is cleared when the account is disconnected; the Google account stays, so the same account connected again finds it.

### files

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/content/comments.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/captions.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/copies.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/files.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/prints.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/source-takes.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/files/week-facts.ts`
- Primary key: `id`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| `tenant_id` | uuid | no |  |  |
| `status` | text | no |  | Where it stands: inbox (waits for a person's word), filed (what Ask may use), set_aside. |
| `source` | text | no |  | Which road brought it: a member's upload, the connected Google profile, the public Google listing, the business's website, or made by Ask on a person's press. |
| `source_ref` | text | yes |  | Where an import read it: the image's address, or Google's name for it, which can expire. Empty for an upload. |
| `name` | text | no |  | What it goes by, to Ask and in the page's words: lower case, hyphens, what it shows first. One per workspace among what is kept. |
| `owner_named` | boolean | no | `false` | A person named it, so the look does not rename it. |
| `mime` | text | no |  |  |
| `bytes` | bigint | no |  |  |
| `width` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `height` | integer | yes |  |  |
| `fingerprint` | text | no |  | sha256 of its first MiB and its size: the same file twice is one row, and a removed one is not imported again (files_let_go). |
| `claude_copy` | jsonb | yes |  | The copy Anthropic holds for reading it: {id, expires_at, width, height}. Service role only, never shown to the model, a member or a tool. |
| `look` | jsonb | yes |  | What the look saw, in contracts FileLook. Written only by file_look_keep. |
| `look_status` | text | no | `'waiting'::text` | waiting, done, refused (the model would not read it, so a person sees it), or failed (no answer; the file stays usable, and the sweep tries again for a week). |
| `look_edition` | integer | yes |  | The edition of the look's rules it was read under (contracts FILE_LOOK_EDITION). A lower one is read again. |
| `looked_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` | When it was last looked at, or tried, or kept: what tells the sweep to leave it alone for a day. |
| `shows` | text | yes |  | Its shelf's word: from the look, Google's category, or a person. owner_shelved says a person chose it. |
| `owner_shelved` | boolean | no | `false` |  |

| `created_by` | uuid | yes |  |  |
| `removed_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | A person removed it: hidden at once. file_purge lets its bytes go and takes the row. |
| `created_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `updated_at` | timestamp with time zone | no | `now()` |  |
| `made` | jsonb | yes |  | How Ask made it (00553): {from, plan}. Empty on everything a person or an import brought. Read by the service role. |
| `kind` | text | no | `'image'::text` | image or video (00556). A video is kept by the video platform; its folder holds only what is made of it. |

| `media_status` | text | yes |  | Where a video stands (00556): uploading (no page or Ask counts it yet), processing, ready, failed. Null for a picture. |

| `sound_said` | text | yes |  | A video's sound in a few words, for the list (contracts soundSaidOf). Written only by file_sound_keep. |

| `copy_used_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the copy at the video platform was last used: played, shown to AI, cut into a video (00654). What is let go first is what was used longest ago. |
| `copy_returned_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When a return of the copy last spent the day's budget (00654 file_copy_return_begin): a workspace's returns of a day are counted from it. |
| `owner_uploaded` | boolean | no | `false` | Its owner uploaded it too (00654): a watched folder's file that an upload met as its twin, written by the upload's door. It is theirs from then on, as any upload: its copy is never let go, and a folder's cleanup never removes it. |
| `superseded_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the item it came from let go of it because the bytes at its provider changed (00654): new bytes are a new file. The seven-day cleanup removes it on the same terms as a tombstone's, and the mark is cleared if an item holds it again. Null: never superseded. |
| `origin_left` | text | yes |  | How a watched file's original left its folder (00657): gone (seen in its provider's bin) or outside (moved out); null while an origin still holds it in. With origin_left_at, its row says the day it leaves the Library. |
| `origin_left_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When a watched file's original left its folder (00657): the newest of its origins' gone_at, where none still holds it in. |

### form_entries

One entry of a website's form (00675; the Forms plan, F0), written with its person and its event in one transaction by form_entry_take: who it is about, the key it came with, the kind of form, the answers as sent, the site's own id for it, a digest of the words, what is owed after it and what each came to (form_entry_settled), how far it got, and when the owner was first told. Never without its person: a person who asked to be forgotten has no entry at all. Goes with its person when they are erased (form_entries_erase_on_contact).

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/forms/links.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/forms/requests.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/people/website-forms.ts`, `packages/db/src/repositories/workspace/export.ts`
- Primary key: `id`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| `form` | text | no |  |  |
| `answers` | jsonb | no |  |  |

| `words` | text | no |  |  |
| `owed` | text[] | no |  | What the entry owes after it, each by its own subscriber: note (what they asked, waiting on their page for Keep), notice (the owner told), confirm (a sign-up with an address that arrived as it was sent is asked to confirm). |

| `state` | text | no | `'accepted'::text` |  |
| `told_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | When the owner first had a notice of the entry (its bell row kept). An accepted entry nobody was told of after ten minutes is paged (apps/edge/lib/website/form-watch.ts). |

### form_entry_links

What happened to one form entry (00680; the Forms plan, 3.1 and 3.5), each written by the act itself: reply (the message sent from the request), conversation (the conversation that arrived with its code, and the message that carried it), visit (a visit asked for from it), marked (a member's word that it was answered another way). Answered is read from here and never kept on the entry: a marked link, a conversation link, or a reply whose message did not fail and was not taken back. ### form_keys

A website's key for the form door (00675; the Forms plan, F0): named, made at random by the dashboard, shown once and kept only as its sha-256, with when it was last used and when it ends. A key changed is a new one, the old one honoured a day. The first key, made from the platform's own key as before 00675, is a row (first, no hash, no name) once a site uses it, so its "last used" shows when the site has moved; it keeps working until it is ended. Members read them; form_key_make, form_key_change and form_key_end write them, and form_entry_take stamps last_used_at.

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/people/website-forms.ts`
- Primary key: `id`
- Row-level security: on, 1 policy

| `first` | boolean | no | `false` |  |

| `last_used_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  |  |
| `ends_at` | timestamp with time zone | yes |  | From when the key is refused: the moment it was ended, or a day after it was changed. Null: it does not end. |
| `site_id` | uuid | yes |  | The site the key proves (00709): set as the key is made, carried to the key it is changed for, and made at the first key's first use. |

### lead_suppressions

By what happened (S8): an email opt-out stops email to that address (calls stay); a customer is hidden from every search; an erasure hides the place, the number and the address for good; a reply read as no (Reach out Part 5) stops the address that said it and, when it is the business's own, the domain (kind domain, the hash of the part after the "@", N6). A bounce is email_state = invalid on the lead, never a row here. The hash is lead_suppression_hash(). The send door's facts, the audience and the finder ask an address through lead_addresses_suppressed.

### post_observations

A post's numbers as its place gave them (00699; the content loop PRD's 5.3 and 9.1): one row per number per read, at an hour, a day, 3, 7 and 28 days after it went up, and at `last`, read by a take-down just before it asks the place (00701; 8.3), since a post's numbers end with it. Each is a running total since it went up; a day's change is two reads apart. availability says why a number is missing (unsupported, delayed, failed, or withheld: a story too few saw), and a missing number is never zero. ### sequence_sends

Decision 0060: one message of a sequence to one person. A customer's (contact_id, no lead_id): queued, then sent, skipped or failed, once. A lead's (lead_id): planned (a time and a mailbox), held while its check doubts it, claimed under the mailbox's day, queued as an email or drafted for its owner, then sent, skipped, failed or handed to the team. A lead's own email (00540) has no sequence, batch or step: a member pressed Send, or said they sent it; it is born queued or sent, the mailbox's day counts it and a reply finds it.

### touches

A known person's reply, comment, reply to a story or coded first message, about a post or through a link (00699; the content loop PRD's Appendix A.1, A.3, A.5): one row per event, once per place by the place's own id. Events, never edited, written by post_comment_keep and touches_keep. The business's own replies and comments are never touches. Emptied with the person (touches_erase_on_contact), moved with a combined record (touches_follow_merge), emptied by age after 180 days except the one that made a person (touches_age_out). Members read.

## Views

Each view's definition is in `supabase/schema.sql`.

### lead_searches_view

Every column of lead_searches with its latest round (round_id, seq, purpose, state, ending, ending_pending, question, answered, target, plan_version, judge_tokens, cost_usd -- what that round has spent, so cost per Qualified lead is read from here -- waiting_since and ended_at) and its counts over the members: qualified (what the Qualified tab shows: a qualified membership once it is counted, lead_member_shown, 00496), review, excluded, counted, emails_checked (a lead Qualified shows whose address was checked and answered) and with_phone (a lead Qualified shows with a number nobody has marked wrong). Excluded members stay counted after their details are blanked, so "40 left out" stays 40. undo_op_id and undo_version name the operation this search's Undo takes while its twenty-four hours run, and are null once it is undone or the day is out. nearby (00145): where to look next when the round ran dry, the nearest ZIP centres past its area, nearest first; [] otherwise. strong, look and long (00146): the leads Qualified shows by fit band, for the band bar over the table. thread_id (00172): the Ask thread the search was planned in, or null. adds_to (00459): the sequence this search's Add goes to. sequence_list (00496): whether this search is a sequence's own list, the one its steps name (sequence_steps.lead_search_id), which the rail draws with the sequences.

- Owned by: `packages/db/src/repositories/leads/workbench.ts`

### usage_ledger

A workspace's metered use, one row per use: each model call (ai_usage, with its dollars), each call's seconds and each WhatsApp conversation opened (the usage events the reports read). Security invoker: a member reads their own workspace's rows.

- Owned by: none
